properties.name: Newgrange
properties.summary: Neolithic passage tomb, older than Stonehenge; the winter solstice sunrise lights the inner chamber.

properties.name: Hill of Tara
properties.summary: Seat of the High Kings in tradition; the Lia Fáil (Stone of Destiny) stands on the hill.

properties.name: Hill of Uisneach
properties.summary: The mythological centre of Ireland and burial place of the goddess Ériu; the Bealtaine fires were lit here.

properties.name: Poulnabrone Dolmen
properties.summary: Portal tomb on the limestone pavement; excavations found the remains of more than 30 people.

properties.name: Caherconnell Stone Fort
properties.summary: Well-preserved ringfort, occupied into the 17th century; sheepdog demonstrations and an active dig.

properties.name: Cliffs of Moher
properties.summary: 214 m sea cliffs; in folklore the lost city of Kilstiffen lies beneath the waves nearby.

properties.name: St Brigid's Well, Liscannor
properties.summary: Holy well with a grotto of offerings; pattern day on the last Sunday of July. Associated with Brigid, goddess and saint.

properties.name: St Brigid's Well, Kildare
properties.summary: Near Brigid's monastery at Kildare; a second, older well lies by the roadside with prayer stones.

properties.name: Clonmacnoise
properties.summary: Monastic city on the Shannon: round towers, high crosses, and the grave slabs of kings.

properties.name: Knocknarea (Queen Maeve's Cairn)
properties.summary: Great cairn said in legend to be the tomb of Queen Medb of Connacht, standing upright facing her enemies.

properties.name: Carrowmore
properties.summary: One of the largest Neolithic cemeteries in Europe, with some 30 surviving tombs.

properties.name: Hook Head
properties.summary: One of the oldest working lighthouses in the world; the monks of Dubhán kept a beacon here from the 5th century.

properties.name: Skellig Michael
properties.summary: Monastic beehive huts on a rock 12 km out in the Atlantic; UNESCO World Heritage Site.

properties.name: Gallarus Oratory
properties.summary: Dry-stone church shaped like an upturned boat, still watertight after a thousand years.

properties.name: Navan Fort (Emain Macha)
properties.summary: Capital of the Ulaid in the Ulster Cycle; home of Conchobar and the Red Branch knights. A huge timber building was built and burned here around 95 BC.
